definition_en: a choice that you make after thinking

senses.title: A choice that is made
senses.definition: a judgement or choice reached after thought
senses.definitionCN: 经过思考后得出的判断或选择
senses.example: The committee reached a decision before noon.

senses.why: A choice becomes a thing once it is spoken and written down.

senses.title: The ability to decide firmly

intro.en: Decision is the Latin noun decisio, a cutting off, from decidere, to cut off.
intro.cn: decision 就是拉丁名词 decisio（切断），来自动词 decidere。

items.en: Decisio named the act of cutting something off.
items.cn: decisio 指把东西切下来的动作。

items.en: It came to mean the settling of a dispute.
items.cn: 后来指争端的了结。

items.en: Décision meant a judgement that ends doubt.
items.cn: décision 指终结疑问的判断。

items.en: Decision entered English as a formal ruling.
items.cn: decision 作为正式的裁定进入英语。

items.en: It now also covers small daily choices.
items.cn: 如今它也指日常里的小选择。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ision ending, and the meaning group runs from a plain choice to a formal verdict.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ision 结尾，近义组则从普通选择走到正式裁断。

entries.definition: the act of separating into parts
the quality of being exact
mockery and laughter at someone
an act of picking one thing
the decision of a court or jury

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stamped page and end with the firmness behind a quick answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一页盖了章的文件开始，落到一个干脆答复背后的那股定力。

normal.en: A decision is a cut that leaves one road behind.
normal.cn: 决定是一刀切下去，把一条路留在身后。

normal.en: Talk is cheap until someone signs the page.
normal.cn: 没人签字之前，话说得再漂亮都不算数。

normal.en: The hardest decisions are the ones with two good answers.
normal.cn: 最难的决定，是两个答案都不错的那种。

normal.en: Decisiveness is speed borrowed from confidence.
normal.cn: 果断是从自信那里借来的速度。

normal.en: A court decision ends the argument but not the feelings.
normal.cn: 法庭的裁决结束了争论，却结束不了情绪。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手把印章按在温热的蜡上。

examples.en: The committee reached a decision before noon.
examples.cn: 委员会中午之前作出了决定。

examples.en: Moving abroad was the hardest decision of her life.
examples.cn: 搬去国外是她一生中最难的决定。

examples.en: The court's decision surprised both sides.
examples.cn: 法院的裁决让双方都感到意外。

root: 来自拉丁名词 decisio（切断），源头是 decidere（切下）。切断绳结的画面先引申为争端的了结与正式裁定，十五世纪进入英语，后来语气放宽，日常小事上的选择也叫 decision。

sensesIntro.en: From a choice put into words, to the firmness that produced it, to a ruling others must obey.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被说成话的选择，到产生它的那份定力，再到别人必须遵从的裁断。

branches.en: The first sense is the choice itself, now fixed in words.

branches.en: The second sense is the inner firmness that makes such choices possible.

branches.en: A private choice and a public ruling share one written form.
branches.cn: 私人选择和公开裁决，共用一种书面形式。

definition_zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的；关键的
definition_en: settling a question or outcome, or showing the ability to decide quickly and firmly
core_image: 一枚砝码落在天平的一端，指针立刻停住，不再摆动
scene: 比赛还剩最后一分钟，他带球突破，一脚把比分定在了终点。Her decisive goal settled the match.
sceneCN: 这里 decisive 指直接决定了结果（第 1 个义项：决定性的）；句意为她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。

pos.zh: 决定性的；果断的；确凿的

senses.title: Settling the outcome
senses.definition: having the power to settle a contest or question
senses.definitionCN: 具有决定比赛或问题结果的力量
senses.example: Her decisive goal settled the match.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个决定性的进球定了胜负。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to cut off'; a decision cuts away the other possibilities, and a decisive act does so in one stroke.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「切掉」；决定切掉其他可能，而 decisive 的行为是一刀切完。

senses.title: Able to decide firmly
senses.definition: of a person, able to choose quickly and without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 指人能迅速选择、毫不犹豫
senses.example: She is decisive under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下很果断。
senses.why: A person who can cut off options does not linger at the fork, and the word praises that speed.
senses.whyCN: 能切掉选项的人不会在岔口徘徊，这个词赞赏的正是这种速度。

senses.title: Conclusive in evidence
senses.definition: of evidence or proof, strong enough to end doubt
senses.definitionCN: 指证据或证明强到足以终结怀疑
senses.example: The fingerprints were decisive evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹是确凿的证据。
senses.why: Proof decides a case the way a verdict decides a trial: once it arrives, argument has nowhere left to go.
senses.whyCN: 证据决定案件，正如裁决决定审判：它一旦出现，争论就无处可去。

senses.title: A battle that ends a war
senses.definition: of a battle or campaign, one that determines the larger outcome
senses.definitionCN: 指决定更大结局的战役或行动
senses.example: The battle was decisive for the whole campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 这场战役对整个战局具有决定性意义。
senses.why: Not every victory changes the war; the word marks the one after which the rest is a formality.
senses.whyCN: 并非每场胜利都改变战争；这个词标记的是那一场之后其余都成形式的胜利。

senses.title: A turning moment
senses.definition: of a moment, the point at which the future is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 指未来在此被固定的时刻
senses.example: That winter was the decisive moment in his career.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天是他事业中的关键时刻。
senses.why: Time has joints, and the word names the one where the limb can bend no other way.
senses.whyCN: 时间有关节，而这个词命名的是那个肢体再也不能向别的方向弯曲的关节。

senses.title: A clear advantage
senses.definition: of an advantage, large or well placed enough to guarantee success
senses.definitionCN: 指优势大到或位置好到足以保证成功
senses.example: Air power gave them a decisive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 空中力量给了他们决定性优势。
senses.why: An advantage is decisive when it cannot be answered by the other side's resources.
senses.whyCN: 当对方的资源无法回应时，优势就是决定性的。

senses.title: A firm tone
senses.definition: of speech, firm and final rather than exploratory
senses.definitionCN: 指言语坚定而最终，而非试探性的
senses.example: He answered in a decisive tone that ended the discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 他用斩钉截铁的语气回答，结束了讨论。
senses.why: Tone can cut a conversation short the way a decision cuts options; nothing is left open.
senses.whyCN: 语气可以像决定切掉选项那样截断对话；没有留下任何开放之处。

senses.title: The determining factor
senses.definition: the element that determines how something else turns out
senses.definitionCN: 决定其他事物如何发展的要素
senses.example: Cost was the decisive factor in the choice.
senses.exampleCN: 成本是这一选择中的决定因素。
senses.why: Among many causes, one is decisive when removing it changes the result.
senses.whyCN: 在众多原因中，当移除某个原因会改变结果时，它就是决定性的。

intro.en: Decisive comes from a Latin verb meaning to cut off, because a decision cuts away alternatives.
intro.cn: decisive 来自一个意为「切掉」的拉丁动词，因为决定就是把其他可能切掉。

items.en: English formed decisive in the 17c. from decision, and applied it to battles, evidence and character alike.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪由 decision 造出 decisive，并把它用于战役、证据与性格。

items.en: Decisio meant 'a cutting off' and also 'a settlement', the moment when a dispute is cut short.
items.cn: decisio 意为「切掉」，也指「了结」，即争端被截断的那一刻。

items.en: Decidere combined de- 'off' with caedere 'to cut', giving 'to cut off, settle'.
items.cn: decidere 由 de-「离开」与 caedere「切」组合，意为「切掉、了结」。

items.en: Caedere 'to cut' also gives cement, incision and concise, all built on cutting.
items.cn: caedere「切」也产生 cement、incision 与 concise，都以「切」为基底。

items.en: The metaphor widened from legal settlement to character: a decisive person is one who can cut off hesitation.
items.cn: 这个比喻从法律了结扩展到性格：果断的人就是能切掉犹豫的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the decision stem; the near-meaning group names kinds of finality.
note.cn: 形近组共享 decision 词干；近义组列出各种终结性。

definition_zh: v. 慷慨陈词；高声演说；朗诵（诗文）；猛烈抨击
definition_en: to speak or recite something loudly and dramatically, as if to an audience
core_image: 一个人站在空房间中央，抬手把句子一句句抛向看不见的听众
scene: 他在台上把台词念得铿锵有力。He began to declaim the opening lines.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：declaim 指朗诵诗文；句意是他开始朗诵开场的那几行。

senses.title: Speak dramatically
senses.definition: to speak loudly and with strong feeling, as if on a stage
senses.definitionCN: 像站在舞台上那样高声而充满感情地讲话
senses.example: He declaimed about the state of the nation.
senses.exampleCN: 他就国家现状慷慨陈词。
senses.why: A room turned into a theatre by one voice.
senses.whyCN: 一个声音把房间变成剧场。

senses.title: Recite aloud
senses.definition: to say a poem or passage aloud with expression
senses.definitionCN: 带感情地大声念出诗歌或段落
senses.example: She declaimed the opening lines.
senses.exampleCN: 她朗诵了开场的那几行。
senses.why: Written lines given breath and volume.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的句子被赋予气息与音量。

senses.title: Attack in speech
senses.definition: to protest strongly against something in public

senses.example: They declaimed against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 他们猛烈抨击新税。
senses.why: A voice thrown against a wall of policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个声音撞向政策的高墙。

intro.en: Declaim comes from Latin declamare, to shout out, from de- plus clamare.
intro.cn: declaim 源自拉丁语 declamare（高声喊出），由 de- 加 clamare 构成。

items.en: Clamare meant to cry out or shout.
items.cn: clamare 意为喊叫。

items.en: Declamare meant to practise public speaking aloud.
items.cn: declamare 意为练习高声公开演说。

items.en: Declame was an early spelling of the verb.
items.cn: declame 是该动词的早期拼法。

items.en: Declaim settled as the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 declaim 定为现代拼法。

items.en: Declaim was used for theatrical recitation.
items.cn: 十七世纪 declaim 用于戏剧式朗诵。

items.en: Declaim gained the sense of pompous speech.
items.cn: 十九世纪 declaim 带上夸夸其谈的意味。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the clam- shouting root; the near-meaning group names loud or formal speech.
note.cn: 形近组共享 clam-（喊叫）词根；近义组都是「高声或正式讲话」的说法。

entries.definition: To cry out suddenly in surprise or anger.

definition_zh: 宣言；声明；申报
definition_en: an official or formal statement
core_image: 广场上被大声念出的那张纸
scene: 代表们站在台阶上，把那份文件读给人群听。The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 declaration 指「宣言」（第 1 个义项：正式公开的声明）；句意是宣言被当众朗读。

pos.zh: 宣言；声明；申报

senses.title: A public formal statement
senses.definition: a formal statement made openly and put on record
senses.definitionCN: 公开作出并被记录下来的正式声明
senses.example: The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 宣言被当众朗读。
senses.why: Saying it in public makes the words hard to take back.
senses.whyCN: 当众说出口，这些话就收不回去了。

senses.title: A statement for customs
senses.definition: a written list of goods or income given to officials
senses.definitionCN: 交给官员的货物或收入清单
senses.example: Fill in the declaration before you reach the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 走到柜台之前先把申报单填好。
senses.why: The state needs a paper version of what you carry.
senses.whyCN: 国家需要你随身带的东西有一份纸质版本。

senses.title: The act of announcing
senses.definition: the act of announcing something officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式宣布某事的行为
senses.example: The declaration of the winner ended the match.
senses.exampleCN: 宣布获胜者终结了这场比赛。
senses.why: Naming an act and naming the paper use one word.
senses.whyCN: 指行为还是指那张纸，用的是同一个词。

intro.en: Declaration is Latin declaratio, from declarare, to make clear, built on clarus, bright.
intro.cn: declaration 即拉丁语 declaratio，来自 declarare（使清楚），根子是 clarus（明亮的）。

items.en: Clarus meant bright and easy to see.
items.cn: clarus 指明亮的、看得清的。

items.en: Declarare meant to make a matter clear to others.
items.cn: declarare 指把事情向别人说清楚。

items.en: Déclaration meant a public statement.
items.cn: déclaration 指公开的声明。

items.en: Declaration entered English as a formal announcement.
items.cn: declaration 作为正式公告进入英语。

items.en: Forms and customs gave it a plain official use.
items.cn: 表格与海关给了它一个朴素的官方用途。

note.en: The look-alike group all end in -ation, and the meaning group names public forms of saying.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -ation 收尾，近义组则列出各种公开说法。

entries.definition: a downward slope or a turning aside
a slowing down in speed
the recovery of land or waste material
something said or written clearly
entries.definitionCN: 清楚说出或写下的内容

an official public declaration

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with words read from a step and end with a form filled in at an airport desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从台阶上念出的文字开始，落到机场柜台前填好的一张表。

normal.en: A declaration is a sentence said where everyone can hear it.
normal.cn: 宣言就是一句在人人听得见的地方说出的话。

normal.en: Paper makes a promise heavier.
normal.cn: 纸让承诺变沉。

normal.en: Declare it once in public and you own it for ever.
normal.cn: 当众讲一次，它就永远归你负责。

normal.en: Customs asks for a list, not a speech.
normal.cn: 海关要的是一张清单，不是一番演讲。

normal.en: Clarus meant bright; a declaration brings a fact into the light.
normal.cn: clarus 本指明亮，宣言就是把事实拿到光下。

abstract.en: Picture a page held up above a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被举在人群上方。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp coming down on a form.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章落在表格上。

abstract.en: Picture a name read out and a room going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被念出，全场安静下来。

examples.en: The declaration was read aloud to the crowd.
examples.cn: 宣言被当众朗读。

examples.en: You must sign the customs declaration at the airport.
examples.cn: 在机场你必须签一份海关申报单。

examples.en: Their declaration of friendship surprised the reporters.
examples.cn: 他们公开的友好声明让记者们感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 declaration 记成「得客来声明」：de 是得，claration 听着像「客来声」，客人一到，主人得公开说一句欢迎。

root: 来自拉丁语 declaratio，动词 declarare 意为「使清楚」，根子是 clarus（明亮的）。十五世纪进入英语时指正式的公开公告，后来也用来指海关申报这类书面说明，以及「宣告」这个动作本身。

sensesIntro.en: From words said aloud in public, to a list handed to officials, to the act behind both.
sensesIntro.cn: 从当众说出的文字，到交给官员的一张清单，再到两者背后的那个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page held up and read out above a crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸在人群上方被举起并朗读。

branches.en: The first sense is the open speech that everyone hears.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是人人听得见的那段公开讲话。

branches.en: The second sense is the same openness pressed into a form.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同样的公开，被压进一张表格里。

branches.en: The third sense is the act that produces either one.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是产生前两者的那个动作。

branches.en: A speech and a form both turn a private fact into a record.
branches.cn: 讲话和表格，都把私事变成了记录。

branches.en: What is declared in words can later be checked against paper.
branches.cn: 口头宣告的东西，日后能拿纸来核对。

intro.en: Declaration belongs to the clar- family: clear, clarify, declare, declarative.
intro.cn: declaration 属于 clar- 这一族：clear、clarify、declare、declarative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is clarus, bright or clear, with clarare meaning to make bright.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 clarus（明亮、清楚），clarare 意为使明亮。

items.example: Undeclared goods were found in the bag.

items.example: Keep the declaration form in your hand.

latinEntries.example: Clarus gives English clear, clarify and declare.

definition_zh: 宣布；声明；申报
definition_en: to say something officially or firmly
core_image: 一个人举起手，向所有人说明一件事
scene: 主席敲了敲桌子，当众说明会议开始。The chair declared the meeting open.
sceneCN: 这里 declare 指「宣布」（第 1 个义项：正式公开地说）；句意是主席宣布会议开始。

pos.zh: 宣布；声明；申报

senses.title: Announce officially
senses.definition: to state something openly in an official way
senses.definitionCN: 以官方的方式公开说明某事
senses.example: The chair declared the meeting open.
senses.exampleCN: 主席宣布会议开始。
senses.why: An official voice turns a private fact into a public one.
senses.whyCN: 官方的声音把私事变成了众人皆知的事。

senses.title: Say firmly
senses.definition: to state a belief with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 很有把握地说出自己的看法
senses.example: She declared that the plan would work.
senses.exampleCN: 她断言这个计划行得通。
senses.why: The word lends a plain sentence the weight of a promise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给一句普通的话添上了承诺的分量。

senses.title: Report goods to customs
senses.definition: to list goods or money to officials
senses.definitionCN: 向官员列出所带的物品或钱款
senses.example: You must declare any cash over the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 超过限额的现金必须申报。
senses.why: What is hidden must be named before it may pass.
senses.whyCN: 藏着的东西，得先被说出来才能通过。

intro.en: Declare came from Latin declarare, to make clear, from clarus, bright.
intro.cn: declare 来自拉丁语 declarare（使清楚），源于 clarus（明亮的）。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, plain and easy to see.
items.cn: clarus 指明亮的、平白易见的。

items.en: Declarare meant to make a matter bright for all to see.
items.cn: declarare 指把事情照亮，让所有人看见。

items.en: Declarer meant to announce or explain openly.
items.cn: declarer 指公开宣布或解释。

items.en: Declare entered English with the sense of making clear.
items.cn: declare 进入英语时，意思是「说清楚」。

items.en: The customs sense grew from the same idea of naming openly.
items.cn: 海关用法也从「公开说出」这个意思长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the opening and closing sounds, and the meaning group runs from telling to proclaiming.

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从敲在桌上的小锤开始，落到海关柜台上打开的一只包。

normal.en: To declare is to switch the light on a fact.
normal.cn: declare 就是给一件事实开灯。

normal.en: The chair says three words and the meeting exists.
normal.cn: 主席说三个词，会议才真正开始。

normal.en: What you declare, you can no longer deny.
normal.cn: 你宣布过的事，就再也否认不了。

normal.en: A customs bag is honest only when it is opened.

normal.en: Clarus meant bright, and declare still means to bring into the light.

abstract.en: Picture a bag unzipped under a bright lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只包在亮灯下被拉开。

examples.en: The chair declared the meeting open.
examples.cn: 主席宣布会议开始。

examples.en: They declared independence in the summer of that year.

examples.en: I have nothing to declare.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 declare 记成「得客来而」：de 是得，clare 听着像「客来而」，客人一到，主人得当众说一声欢迎。

sensesIntro.en: From an official word that starts a meeting, to a firm belief, to goods named at a border.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让会议开始的那句官方话，到坚定的看法，再到在关口说清的物品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand making one fact public.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手举起，把一件事变成公开的。

branches.en: The first sense is the official voice that changes a situation.

intro.en: Declare and its noun declaration carry the whole clar- family of clearness.

latinIntro.en: The root is clarus, bright; clarare meant to make bright.

definition_zh: 下降；衰退；婉拒
definition_en: to become smaller or weaker; to refuse politely
core_image: 一条缓缓下滑的曲线
scene: 入冬后游客少了，街上的小店一间间关了门。Sales declined sharply after the summer.
sceneCN: 这里 decline 指「下降」（第 1 个义项：数量变少）；句意是夏天过后销量急剧下滑。

pos.zh: 下降；衰退；婉拒
下降；衰退

senses.title: Become less in number
senses.definition: to fall in number, amount or strength
senses.definitionCN: 数量、数额或力量变小
senses.example: Sales declined sharply after the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天过后销量急剧下滑。
senses.why: A line that turns downward is the plainest sign of loss.
senses.whyCN: 曲线往下一拐，是最直白的损失信号。

senses.title: Refuse politely
senses.definition: to say no to an offer in a courteous way
senses.definitionCN: 有礼貌地回绝别人的提议
senses.example: She declined the invitation with a short note.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一封短笺婉拒了邀请。
senses.why: To bend away from a request is gentler than to reject it.
senses.whyCN: 从请求旁边弯开去，比直接推开要温和。

senses.title: A slow loss of strength
senses.definition: a gradual weakening of health, power or quality
senses.definitionCN: 健康、实力或品质逐渐变弱
senses.example: The town's decline began when the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场关闭后，这座小镇开始衰落。
senses.why: Small losses, repeated, become a state you can name.
senses.whyCN: 细小的损失反复发生，就成了可以命名的一种状态。

intro.en: Decline came from Latin declinare, to bend away, from clinare, to bend.
intro.cn: decline 来自拉丁语 declinare（弯开），源于 clinare（弯曲）。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or lean.
items.cn: clinare 指弯曲或倾斜。

items.en: Declinare meant to bend away from a straight line.
items.cn: declinare 指偏离直线弯向一边。

items.en: Decliner covered both sinking and turning aside.
items.cn: decliner 既指下沉，也指让到一边。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line bending down and end with an offer gently put aside.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条向下弯的线开始，落到被轻轻放到一边的提议。

normal.cn: 小镇是一间店一间店地衰落的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decline 记成「低可赖」：de 是低，cline 像「靠」，坡一低，人就只能靠着往下溜。

root: 源自拉丁语 declinare（弯开、偏斜），词根 clinare 意为弯曲。它的两个主要意思都从「弯」来：数字往下弯是下降，人往旁边弯是婉拒；语法上的变格用法也沿用同一个比喻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line bending downward, to an offer bent aside, to a long state of weakening.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向下弯的线，到被让开的提议，再到长期变弱的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line easing gently downward across a page.

branches.en: The first sense is quantity dropping on a chart.

branches.en: The second sense is a person stepping politely aside.

branches.en: The third sense is a long slope that no single fall explains.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一道慢坡，单次下跌解释不了。

branches.en: A small fall repeated becomes a long decline.
branches.cn: 一次小跌反复发生，就成了长期衰退。

branches.en: To decline an offer is to let it fall away from you.

intro.cn: decline 带着 -clin- 词干，与 incline、recline、declination 同族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is clinare, to bend; Greek had a related word for a bed, kline.

intro.en: Declivity comes from Latin declivitas, from declivis, sloping down, from de- plus clivus.
intro.cn: declivity 源自拉丁语 declivitas，来自 declivis（向下倾斜），由 de- 加 clivus（坡）构成。

definition_zh: 分解；腐烂；使腐败
definition_en: to break something down into simpler parts or substances
core_image: 一块木头在湿土里一年年变软、变空、最后消失
scene: 雨后的林地里，倒木正在慢慢瓦解：Fungi decompose the fallen trunk until only a dark line of soil remains.
sceneCN: 这里 decompose 是「分解、腐烂」（第 2 个义项：有机物被真菌分解）；句意：真菌分解这根倒下的树干，最后只剩一道深色的土痕。

pos.zh: 使分解；使腐烂；拆解（使某物分解）
分解；腐烂；崩解（自行分解）

senses.title: Split a compound chemically
senses.definition: to separate a compound into simpler substances by chemical action
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学作用把化合物分离成更简单的物质
senses.example: Strong heat decomposes the carbonate into oxide and gas.
senses.exampleCN: 高温把这种碳酸盐分解为氧化物和气体。
senses.why: The verb undoes a combination: de- takes apart what compose had put together.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把「组合」拆掉：de- 把 compose 曾经放在一起的东西分开。

senses.title: Rot away
senses.definition: of dead organic matter, to decay into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 指死亡的有机物腐烂成更简单的物质
senses.example: The leaves decompose faster when the soil stays moist.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤保持湿润时，落叶分解得更快。
senses.why: Decay is chemical decomposition happening without a flask, carried out by microbes and water.
senses.whyCN: 腐败就是没有烧瓶的化学分解，由微生物与水来完成。

senses.title: Make something rot
senses.definition: to cause organic material to decay, used with a subject that acts on the object
senses.definitionCN: 使有机材料腐烂，主语对宾语施加作用
senses.example: Bacteria decompose the manure before the field is planted.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在整地之前把粪肥分解掉。
senses.why: The transitive use adds an agent: someone or something sets the breakdown going.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加了施动者：某人或某物让分解开始发生。

senses.title: Split a mathematical object
senses.definition: to express a function, matrix or number as a product or sum of simpler parts
senses.definitionCN: 把函数、矩阵或数表示成更简单部分的乘积或和
senses.example: The program decomposes the matrix before solving the system.
senses.exampleCN: 程序在求解方程组之前先把矩阵分解。
senses.why: Mathematics reuses the verb because the operation is a structured taking-apart, not physical decay.
senses.whyCN: 数学复用这个动词，因为该操作是结构化的拆分，而不是物理腐败。

senses.title: Divide a problem into parts
senses.definition: in computing, to divide a task or system into smaller parts that can be handled separately
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把任务或系统划分成可分别处理的更小部分
senses.example: We decompose the pipeline into stages that can run in parallel.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这条流水线拆成可以并行运行的若干阶段。
senses.why: Software work repeats the same gesture at the level of tasks, where the parts are functions rather than molecules.
senses.whyCN: 软件工作在任务层面重复同一动作，只是拆出的部分成了功能而不是分子。

senses.title: Take an argument apart
senses.definition: to analyse a text or argument by separating its claims and assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 通过分离主张与假设来分析文本或论证
senses.example: The class decomposed the editorial into three unsupported claims.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂上把这篇社论拆解成三个缺乏支持的断言。
senses.why: Analytical reading is decomposition in the mind, where the pieces are claims rather than compounds.
senses.whyCN: 分析性阅读是心智中的分解，拆出的碎片是论点而不是化合物。

senses.title: Break down after death
senses.definition: of a body, to pass through the stages of post-mortem breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 指尸体经历死后的各个崩解阶段
senses.example: The body had decomposed for weeks before it was found.
senses.exampleCN: 尸体被发现时已经分解了数周。
senses.why: Forensic writing uses the verb for the whole sequence, keeping the tone clinical rather than emotional.
senses.whyCN: 法医写作使用这个动词描述整个序列，语气保持临床化而非情绪化。

senses.title: Fall apart figuratively
senses.definition: of an organisation, plan or relationship, to disintegrate gradually
senses.definitionCN: 指组织、计划或关系逐渐瓦解
senses.example: The coalition decomposed into rival factions within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联盟在一年之内瓦解成相互对立的派系。
senses.why: The image of a structure losing its bonds transfers easily to institutions that lose their internal ties.
senses.whyCN: 「结构失去结合」的形象很容易移用到失去内部纽带的机构上。

intro.en: Decompose was formed in French chemistry and then borrowed into English; its Latin parts are de- and componere.
intro.cn: decompose 在法国化学中形成，随后借入英语；其拉丁语成分是 de- 与 componere。

items.en: Compose comes from Latin componere 'to put together', from com- 'together' and ponere 'to place'. The same ponere underlies position, deposit, impose and postpone.
items.cn: compose 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「共同」与 ponere「放置」构成。同一个 ponere 也是 position、deposit、impose、postpone 的词根。

items.en: In de- the prefix carries the sense 'apart, away, down', so the new verb means to undo a putting-together.
items.cn: 前缀 de- 带有「分开、离开、向下」之意，因此新动词表示「撤销一次组合」。

items.en: French décomposer is recorded in eighteenth-century chemical writing, when analysts were learning to split compounds into elements. English adopted the verb soon after.
items.cn: 法语 décomposer 见于 18 世纪的化学写作，当时分析家正学着把化合物拆成元素。英语很快借入了这个动词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology applied decompose to rotting organisms, giving the everyday sense its scientific footing.
items.cn: 19 世纪的生物学把 decompose 用于腐烂的生物体，使这个日常义项获得科学依据。

items.en: Mathematics and computing later borrowed the verb for structured splitting, while figurative use for failing institutions followed naturally. The first recorded date of each extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 数学与计算随后借用这个动词表示结构化拆分，用于失败机构的比喻用法也自然跟进。各个延伸义项的确切首见年代尚无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the root; the second holds other verbs of breaking down.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根；第二组是其他表示「崩解」的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result; decompose is the action that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；decompose 是产生这一过程的动作。

entries.definition: To put together or create; decompose reverses exactly that direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西组合起来或创作；decompose 正是把这一方向反过来。

entries.definition: The organism or device doing the work; it cannot replace the verb in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；不能用来替代句中的动词。

entries.definition: To decay naturally, often with a smell; decompose is the neutral term used in science.
entries.definitionCN: 自然腐烂，常带气味；decompose 是科学中的中性说法。

entries.definition: A general phrasal verb for failure or separation, applied to machines and emotions as well as matter.
entries.definitionCN: 通用短语动词，表示故障或分离，可用于机器、情绪与物质。

entries.definition: To break into fragments, often violently or completely; decompose stresses chemical change rather than mechanical shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 碎成小块，常含剧烈或彻底之意；decompose 强调化学变化而非机械碎裂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the reversal prefix and the verb forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表反转的前缀与动词形式。

normal.en: compose = put together; decompose = take apart.
normal.cn: compose 是放在一起，decompose 是拆开。

normal.en: The forms follow the regular pattern: decomposes, decomposed, decomposing.
normal.cn: 词形变化规律：decomposes、decomposed、decomposing。

normal.en: The object tells you the sense: decompose a compound, a leaf, a matrix, a problem.
normal.cn: 看宾语就能判断义项：分解化合物、落叶、矩阵或问题。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' links it to position, deposit and impose.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」把它与 position、deposit、impose 联系起来。

normal.en: The soil under a fallen log is the word's home ground.
normal.cn: 倒木下面的土壤，就是这个词的主场。

abstract.en: Think of a knot loosening thread by thread until the rope is only fibre.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结一根线一根线地松开，直到绳子只剩纤维。

abstract.en: A decomposing log is a book whose pages are being returned to the library of the forest.
abstract.cn: 分解中的倒木是一本书，书页正被还给森林的图书馆。

abstract.en: When a team decomposes a task, it is rotting the workload on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当团队拆分任务时，他们是在有意让工作量「腐烂」掉。

examples.en: Plastic does not decompose easily, which is why it persists in the ocean.
examples.cn: 塑料不易分解，这正是它在海洋中持久存在的原因。

examples.en: The enzyme helps bacteria decompose cellulose in the rumen.
examples.cn: 这种酶帮助细菌分解瘤胃中的纤维素。

examples.en: We decompose the workflow into steps that can be tested separately.
examples.cn: 我们把工作流拆成可以分别测试的步骤。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（拆）+ compose（组成）→ 把组成拆掉 → 分解、腐烂

root: 拉丁语 de-「分开、向下」+ componere「放在一起」（com- + ponere「放置」）；经法语 décomposer 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one action: undoing a structured whole, whether by heat, microbes, mathematics, code, analysis, death or collapse.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：把有结构的整体拆开，手段可以是加热、微生物、数学、代码、分析、死亡或崩解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bonds loosening until a whole becomes simpler pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：结合逐渐松开，整体变成更简单的碎片。

branches.en: THE CORE: a compound or a dead body comes apart into simpler substances.
branches.cn: 核心：化合物或尸体拆解为更简单的物质。

branches.en: THE AGENT: a subject can make the breakdown happen, shifting the verb to transitive use.
branches.cn: 施动者：主语可使分解发生，动词由此转为及物用法。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: mathematics and computing split objects and tasks by design.
branches.cn: 结构：数学与计算按设计把对象和任务拆开。

branches.en: THE TEXT: an argument is taken apart into claims and assumptions.
branches.cn: 文本：论证被拆成主张与假设。

branches.en: THE END: a body passes through post-mortem stages, and an institution loses its internal bonds.
branches.cn: 终点：尸体经历死后阶段，机构失去内部纽带。

intro.en: Decompose is a reversal prefix on a verb of putting together.
intro.cn: decompose 是在「组合」动词上加表反转的前缀。

latinIntro.en: The elements are de- 'apart' and ponere 'place', the second reached through French composer rather than direct Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是 de-「分开」与 ponere「放置」，后者经法语 composer 而非直接从拉丁语进入。

items.example: A decomposer returns nutrients to the soil.
items.exampleCN: 分解者把养分归还土壤。

items.example: The material is decomposable within one season.
items.exampleCN: 这种材料一个季节内即可分解。
若干物种构成了这个群落。

items.example: The position of the log affects how it decomposes.
items.exampleCN: 倒木的位置会影响它的分解方式。

items.example: The flood deposited silt over the floodplain.
items.exampleCN: 洪水在泛滥平原上沉积了淤泥。

items.example: The new rule imposes a cost on polluters.
items.exampleCN: 新规给污染者施加了成本。

definition_zh: 分解；腐烂；拆解
definition_en: the process of breaking something down into simpler parts or substances
core_image: 一块落叶在土里慢慢裂成看不见的碎片
scene: 落叶层下，微生物正在悄悄工作：Bacterial decomposition turns the fallen leaves into dark soil within a year.
sceneCN: 这里 decomposition 是「分解、腐烂」（第 2 个义项：有机物被微生物分解）；句意：细菌分解在一年之内把落叶变成深色土壤。

pos.zh: 分解；腐烂；降解；拆解（不可数，特定语境可作可数）

forms.label: 施动名词（分解者；分解装置）

derivatives.zh: 组成；作品；构成（同词根反向词）

senses.title: Breaking a compound apart
senses.definition: a chemical reaction in which a compound splits into simpler substances
senses.definitionCN: 化合物裂解为更简单物质的化学反应
senses.example: Heating limestone causes the decomposition of calcium carbonate.
senses.exampleCN: 加热石灰石会导致碳酸钙分解。
senses.why: de- means apart and composition means putting together, so the noun names the undoing of a chemical combination.
senses.whyCN: de- 表示「分开」，composition 表示「放在一起」，因此这个名词指把化学组合拆开。

senses.title: Rotting of dead matter
senses.definition: the process by which dead plants or animals decay into simpler matter
senses.definitionCN: 死亡动植物腐烂为更简单物质的过程
senses.example: Decomposition of the fallen log took nearly a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这根倒木的分解花了将近十年。
senses.why: Living bodies are built from compounds, so their decay is chemically the same undoing of combinations.
senses.whyCN: 活体由化合物构成，因此它们的腐败在化学上就是同样的「拆解组合」。

senses.title: An ecosystem process
senses.definition: the ecological process that returns carbon and nutrients from dead matter to the environment
senses.definitionCN: 把碳与养分从死亡有机物归还环境的生态过程
senses.example: Decomposition in tropical soils is fast because of heat and moisture.
senses.exampleCN: 热带土壤中的分解因高温与湿润而很快。
senses.why: Ecology treats the same chemistry as a system function, measured by rates and nutrient budgets.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把同一套化学当作系统功能，用速率与养分收支来衡量。

senses.title: Breaking down a mathematical object
senses.definition: the splitting of a function, matrix or graph into simpler components
senses.definitionCN: 把函数、矩阵或图拆成更简单成分
senses.example: The algorithm relies on a matrix decomposition that costs little memory.
senses.exampleCN: 该算法依赖一种占用内存很少的矩阵分解。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the word because the operation is literally a structured breaking-apart of a whole.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个词，因为该操作确实是把整体按结构拆开。

senses.title: Splitting a system into modules
senses.definition: in computing, the division of a problem or system into smaller independent parts
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域把问题或系统划分为更小的独立部分
senses.example: Good decomposition keeps each module testable on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的系统拆分让每个模块都能独立测试。
senses.why: Software design repeats the chemical image at a higher level: a complex whole is easier to handle in parts.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计在更高层次重复了化学的意象：复杂的整体拆成部分更好处理。

senses.title: Taking an argument apart
senses.definition: the analytical separation of a text, argument or idea into its components
senses.definitionCN: 把文本、论证或观点分析性地拆成若干成分
senses.example: Her decomposition of the speech showed how the argument shifted halfway.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这篇演讲的拆解显示出论证在中途如何转向。
senses.why: Analysis is mental decomposition, and the noun marks the structured separation rather than the decay.
senses.whyCN: 分析就是心智上的分解，这个名词标记的是有条理的拆分，而不是腐败。

senses.title: Stages after death
senses.definition: in forensic science, the sequence of changes by which a body breaks down after death
senses.definitionCN: 法医学中尸体死后逐步崩解的阶段序列
senses.example: Insect evidence placed the decomposition stage at about two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 昆虫证据把这一分解阶段判断在两周左右。
senses.why: Forensic taphonomy needs a neutral word for the whole sequence, avoiding the vaguer everyday term decay.
senses.whyCN: 法医埋藏学需要一个中性的词来描述整个序列，避开含混的日常词 decay。

senses.title: Release of nutrients
senses.definition: the release of soluble nutrients into soil or water as dead matter breaks down
senses.definitionCN: 死亡有机物崩解时把可溶养分释放到土壤或水中
senses.example: Decomposition released enough nitrate to feed the next crop.
senses.exampleCN: 分解释放的硝酸盐足以供养下一季作物。
senses.why: This sense focuses on the output rather than the process, since the breakdown is valued for what it gives back.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项聚焦于产出而非过程，因为人们看重分解，正是看重它归还了什么。

intro.en: Decomposition undoes a Latin putting-together; the English word may have been borrowed from French rather than built in English.
intro.cn: decomposition 把拉丁语的「放在一起」拆开；这个英语词可能借自法语，而不是在英语内部构造的。

items.en: Composition comes from Latin componere, 'to put together', made of com- 'together' and ponere 'to place'. The root ponere also yields position, deposit and impose.
items.cn: composition 来自拉丁语 componere「放在一起」，由 com-「共同」与 ponere「放置」构成。词根 ponere 还产生 position、deposit 与 impose。

items.en: The prefix de- here means 'down, apart, away', the same reversal force it has in detach and decline.
items.cn: 此处前缀 de- 表示「向下、分开、离开」，与它在 detach、decline 中的反转意味相同。

items.en: French chemists formed decomposer in the eighteenth century for the separation of compound substances. English decompose and decomposition followed, probably through French rather than directly from Latin.
items.cn: 法国化学家在 18 世纪造出 decomposer，用于描述化合物物质的分离。英语的 decompose 与 decomposition 随之出现，大概是经法语而不是直接从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: With the rise of ecology, decomposition was applied to the decay of dead organisms and the cycling of nutrients. The exact date of this shift is not firmly established.
items.cn: 随着生态学兴起，decomposition 被用于描述死亡有机体的腐败与养分循环。这一转变的确切年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century mathematics and computing extended the word to the structured splitting of matrices, functions, systems and problems.
items.cn: 20 世纪的数学与计算把这个词扩展到矩阵、函数、系统与问题的结构化拆分。

note.en: The first group is built on the same root; the second holds related breakdown processes.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一词根上；第二组是相关的崩解过程。

entries.definition: The action itself; decomposition is the process noun derived from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指动作本身；decomposition 是由它派生的过程名词。

entries.definition: The putting together of parts, or the resulting whole; decomposition undoes exactly that.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分放在一起，或由此形成的整体；decomposition 正是把这一过程反过来。

entries.definition: An organism or device that carries out decomposition; the noun ending -er marks the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 执行分解的生物或装置；-er 词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: Slow natural rotting, often with a negative tone; decomposition is the neutral scientific term.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的自然腐烂，常带负面色彩；decomposition 是中性科学术语。

entries.definition: A general failure or separation, usable for machines, health or chemistry; decomposition is more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指故障或分离，可用于机器、健康或化学；decomposition 更具体。

entries.definition: Anaerobic rotting of protein-rich matter with a strong smell; a narrower, more graphic kind of decomposition.
entries.definitionCN: 富含蛋白质的物质在缺氧条件下的腐烂，气味强烈；是分解中更窄、更具体的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the de-/com- reversal and the scientific collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：de- 与 com- 的反向关系以及科学搭配。

normal.en: composition puts together; decomposition takes apart. The prefixes do the work.
normal.cn: composition 把东西放在一起，decomposition 把它们拆开，起作用的是两个前缀。

normal.en: The family runs decompose, decomposer, decomposable, decomposition.
normal.cn: 同族词有 decompose、decomposer、decomposable、decomposition。

normal.en: Standard phrases mark the fields: organic decomposition, thermal decomposition, rate of decomposition.
normal.cn: 标准搭配标出领域：有机物分解、热分解、分解速率。

normal.en: The root ponere 'place' also hides in position, deposit and impose.
normal.cn: 词根 ponere「放置」也藏在 position、deposit、impose 里。

normal.en: A leaf turning into soil is the image that fits both the garden and the laboratory.
normal.cn: 叶子变成土壤的画面，既适合花园，也适合实验室。

abstract.en: Think of a Lego castle being taken apart brick by brick, with each brick still usable.
abstract.cn: 想象一座乐高城堡被一块块拆开，每块砖仍能继续使用。

abstract.en: A fallen tree is a bank account that decomposition pays out slowly.
abstract.cn: 倒下的树是一个账户，分解在慢慢把存款付出去。

abstract.en: In code, decomposition is the same gesture: a big block split into pieces you can carry.
abstract.cn: 在代码里，分解是同一个动作：把大块拆成你能拿得动的小块。

examples.en: The rate of decomposition depends on temperature, water and oxygen.
examples.cn: 分解速率取决于温度、水分与氧气。

examples.en: Thermal decomposition of the sample released a colourless gas.
examples.cn: 样品的热分解释放出一种无色气体。

examples.en: The team's decomposition of the problem made the code far easier to test.
examples.cn: 团队对问题的拆分使代码更容易测试。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（去掉）+ composition（组合）→ 把组合拆掉 → 分解、腐烂

root: 拉丁语 de-「分开、向下」+ compositio「组合」，后者来自 componere（com-「共同」+ ponere「放置」）；经法语 décomposer 进入英语，形成 decompose 与 decomposition。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a whole coming apart: a compound, a body, an ecosystem, a matrix, a system, a text, a corpse, a nutrient store.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「整体拆开」：化合物、尸体、生态系统、矩阵、系统、文本、遗体、养分库。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structured whole losing its bonds and falling into simpler pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个有结构的整体失去结合，散成更简单的碎片。

branches.en: THE CORE: a chemical combination is undone, whether in a flask or in a dead body.
branches.cn: 核心：化学组合被拆开，无论是在烧瓶里还是在尸体里。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: the process is studied for its rate and for the nutrients it releases.
branches.cn: 生态系统：人们研究这一过程的速率，以及它释放的养分。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: mathematics splits functions, matrices and graphs into simpler parts.
branches.cn: 对象：数学把函数、矩阵与图拆成更简单的部分。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: computing splits problems into modules that can be handled separately.
branches.cn: 系统：计算把问题拆成可分别处理的模块。

branches.en: THE READING: an argument can be taken apart for analysis, and a corpse for forensic reconstruction.
branches.cn: 解读：论证可被拆解以供分析，尸体可被拆解以供法医重建。

intro.en: Decomposition is a prefix of reversal plus a noun of putting together.
intro.cn: decomposition 是一个表示反转的前缀加上一个表示「组合」的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are de- 'apart' and componere 'to put together' (com- + ponere 'place'), with the noun ending -itio giving English -ition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 de-「分开」与 componere「放在一起」（com- + ponere「放置」），名词词尾 -itio 在英语中变为 -ition。

items.example: Decomposition of the litter is fastest in warm, wet soil.
items.exampleCN: 枯落物的分解在温暖湿润的土壤中最快。

items.meaning: an agent that breaks matter down
items.example: Fungi are the main decomposers of wood.
items.exampleCN: 真菌是木材的主要分解者。

items.example: The packaging is fully decomposable in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种包装在土壤中可完全分解。

items.meaning: a putting together; the whole so formed
items.example: The composition of the soil affects decomposition.

items.meaning: a place where something is set
items.example: Position and composition share one Latin root.
items.exampleCN: position 与 composition 共享一个拉丁词根。

items.example: The river deposit holds partly decomposed matter.
items.exampleCN: 河流沉积物中含有部分分解的物质。

items.example: Impose and decompose share the root ponere.
items.exampleCN: impose 与 decompose 共享词根 ponere。

definition_zh: n. 减压；降低压力；（潜水后）减压停留；（数据）解压缩
definition_en: a reduction in pressure, or the process of returning compressed data to its original form
core_image: 一个被压紧的弹簧慢慢松开，潜水员在浅处停着让体内气泡一点点散掉
scene: 潜水员在浅处停着慢慢减压。The diver began a slow decompression.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：decompression 指潜水后的减压；句意是潜水员开始缓慢减压。

pos.zh: 减压；降低压力；减压停留；数据解压缩

senses.title: A drop in pressure
senses.definition: a reduction of physical pressure on something
senses.definitionCN: 作用在某物上的物理压力减小
senses.example: Decompression let the gas escape slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 减压让气体慢慢逸出。
senses.why: A tight grip loosened by degrees.
senses.whyCN: 紧握的手一点点松开。

senses.title: The slow ascent of a diver
senses.definition: the staged release of pressure after a deep dive
senses.definitionCN: 深潜之后分阶段释放压力
senses.example: The diver began a slow decompression.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员开始缓慢减压。
senses.why: Bubbles leaving the blood before the surface.
senses.whyCN: 气泡在到达水面前先离开血液。

senses.title: Unpacking data
senses.definition: the process of restoring compressed files to full size
senses.definitionCN: 把压缩文件还原成原始大小
senses.example: Decompression took only a second.
senses.exampleCN: 解压缩只花了一秒。
senses.why: A folded file opened back to its shape.
senses.whyCN: 折起的文件重新展开成原样。

intro.en: Decompression is de- plus compression, from Latin comprimere, to press together.
intro.cn: decompression 由 de- 加 compression 构成，后者源自拉丁语 comprimere（压在一起）。

items.en: Premere meant to press.
items.cn: premere 意为压。

items.en: Comprimere meant to press together.
items.cn: comprimere 意为压在一起。

items.en: Compress entered English for pressing into less space.
items.cn: 十四世纪 compress 以压入更小空间义进入英语。

items.en: Compression named the act of pressing together.
items.cn: compression 指压在一起的行为。

items.en: Decompression was used for releasing steam pressure.
items.cn: 十九世纪 decompression 用于释放蒸汽压力。

items.en: Decompression became a diving and computing term.
items.cn: 二十世纪 decompression 成为潜水与计算机术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the press- family; the near-meaning group names release from pressure or packing.
note.cn: 形近组同属 press- 家族；近义组都是「从压力或压缩中释放」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of pressing something into less space.
To reduce pressure or unpack data.
To press down or make someone sad.
The act of setting something free.
The process of becoming larger.
Taking things out of a packed container.
The process of becoming less tight or tense.

normalIntro.en: Decompression is de- plus compression: undo the pressing.
normalIntro.cn: decompression 就是 de- 加 compression：把压紧的状态解开。

normal.en: Press means to push hard.
normal.cn: press 意为用力压。

normal.en: Compress presses things together.
normal.cn: compress 把东西压到一起。

normal.en: Compression is the pressed state.
normal.cn: compression 是被压紧的状态。

normal.en: De- reverses the pressing.
normal.cn: de- 把压紧反转过来。

normal.en: Decompression lets it all out.
normal.cn: decompression 让一切释放出来。

abstract.en: A tight grip loosened by degrees.
abstract.cn: 紧握的手一点点松开。

abstract.en: Bubbles leaving the blood before the surface.
abstract.cn: 气泡在到达水面前先离开血液。

abstract.en: A folded file opened back to its shape.
abstract.cn: 折起的文件重新展开成原样。

examples.en: Rapid decompression can injure a diver.
examples.cn: 快速减压会伤害潜水员。

examples.en: The chamber provides controlled decompression.
examples.cn: 这个舱提供可控的减压。

examples.en: File decompression finished without errors.
examples.cn: 文件解压缩顺利完成，没有报错。

dict_mnemonic.text: decompression 谐音「弟康普瑞申」——不如记 de（去掉）＋ compression（压缩）＝把压缩去掉，「减压、解压缩」。

root: 拉丁语 premere（压）→ comprimere（压在一起）→ 英语 compression（压缩）→ decompression（减压）

sensesIntro.en: One loosened grip: pressure, the ascent of a diver and a packed file.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一只松开的手：压力、潜水员的上浮与打包的文件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightened spring slowly opening back to its own length
core.cn: 核心意象：被压紧的弹簧慢慢松开，回到自己的长度

branches.en: A tight grip loosened by degrees.
branches.cn: 紧握的手一点点松开。

branches.en: Bubbles leaving the blood before the surface.
branches.cn: 气泡在到达水面前先离开血液。

branches.en: A folded file opened back to its shape.
branches.cn: 折起的文件重新展开成原样。

branches.en: Both release stored pressure safely and slowly.
branches.cn: 两者都缓慢而安全地释放储存的压力。

branches.en: Both return something squeezed back to its original size.
branches.cn: 两者都把被挤压的东西还原到原来的大小。

intro.en: Decompression is de- plus com- plus press plus -ion; the pressing family is very productive.
intro.cn: decompression 由 de- 加 com- 加 press 再加 -ion 构成；压这个家族构词能力很强。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere means to press and pandere means to spread out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为压，pandere 意为展开。

definition_zh: 装饰；装修；授勋
definition_en: to make something look more attractive by adding things to it
core_image: 门上挂起的一串红纸灯
scene: 过年前，家家户户在门上贴红纸、挂灯笼。They decorate the house with red paper every year.
sceneCN: 这里 decorate 指「装饰」（第 1 个义项：加东西使好看）；句意是他们每年用红纸装饰屋子。

pos.zh: 装饰；装修；授勋

senses.title: Add things to make it beautiful
senses.definition: to put ornaments or colour on something to improve its look
senses.definitionCN: 把饰物或颜色加到东西上，使其更好看
senses.example: They decorate the house with red paper every year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年用红纸装饰屋子。
senses.why: A plain surface is given a dress for a special day.
senses.whyCN: 光秃的表面，为特别的日子换上了一身衣服。

senses.title: Paint and fit a building
senses.definition: to put paper, paint or fittings into a room
senses.definitionCN: 给房间贴纸、刷漆或装设备
senses.example: We decorated the kitchen last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去年春天装修了厨房。
senses.why: A house is dressed inside as well as out.
senses.whyCN: 房子里面和外面，都要穿衣服。

senses.title: Give a medal or honour
senses.definition: to give someone an honour or a medal
senses.definitionCN: 把荣誉或奖章授予某人
senses.example: The officer was decorated for saving two men.
senses.exampleCN: 这名军官因救下两人而受勋。
senses.why: Honour is also something pinned on, like an ornament.
senses.whyCN: 荣誉也是别在身上的一样东西，和饰物很像。

intro.en: Decorate came from Latin decorare, to adorn, from decus, honour and beauty.
intro.cn: decorate 来自拉丁语 decorare（装点），源于 decus（荣誉与美）。

items.en: Decus meant honour, grace and beauty.
items.cn: decus 指荣誉、优雅与美。

items.en: Decorare meant to add honour or beauty to a thing.
items.cn: decorare 指给事物添上荣誉或美。

items.en: Décorer carried the sense of adorning a place.
items.cn: décorer 带着装点某个场所的意思。

items.en: Decorate entered English for adorning rooms and altars.
items.cn: decorate 进入英语，用于装点房间与祭坛。

items.en: The military sense of a decoration came later.
items.cn: 表示勋章的那个用法是后来才有的。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dec- opening, and the meaning group names ways of adding beauty.
note.cn: 形近组都以 dec- 开头，近义组则列出添美的几种说法。

entries.definition: to announce something officially
to give time or effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或精力献给某个目的

entries.definition: polite and correct in behaviour
to make something more beautiful
to add decoration to something
to make a place look better

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with red paper on a door and end with a medal pinned to a coat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门上的红纸开始，落到别在外套上的一枚奖章。

normal.en: A plain door waits all year for one red sheet.
normal.cn: 一扇素门，等一整年就为一张红纸。

normal.en: Decorating is putting a day's clothes on a room.
normal.cn: 装饰，就是给房间穿上过节的衣服。

normal.en: Paint is cheaper than moving house.
normal.cn: 刷一遍漆，比搬家便宜。

normal.en: The same word dresses a room and honours a soldier.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既打扮房间，也为士兵授勋。

normal.en: Decus meant honour, so decoration was never only about looks.
normal.cn: decus 本指荣誉，所以装饰从来不只是好看。

abstract.en: Picture a row of lanterns going up along a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一排灯笼沿着墙挂起来。

abstract.en: Picture a brush moving over a bare wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刷子在一面素墙上来回移动。

abstract.en: Picture a pin being fixed to a dark coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚别针被别在深色外套上。

examples.en: They decorate the house with red paper every year.
examples.cn: 他们每年用红纸装饰屋子。

examples.en: The hall was decorated with flowers for the wedding.
examples.cn: 大厅为了婚礼用鲜花装饰起来。

examples.en: He was decorated for bravery after the fire.
examples.cn: 那场火灾之后他因英勇而受勋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decorate 记成「得客 rated」：de 是得，corate 听着像「客 rated」，客人来了要给好评，先把屋子装饰漂亮。

root: 来自拉丁语 decorare（装点），源于 decus（荣誉、体面、美）。十五世纪进入英语时指装点房间与祭坛，后来引申为粉刷装修房屋；因为「荣誉」本就带在身上，授勋的用法也从同一源头长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From brightening a surface for a day, to fitting out a room, to pinning honour on a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从为一天把表面打扮起来，到把房间装备好，再到把荣誉别在人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red paper and lanterns going up on a plain door.
core.cn: 核心意象：红纸与灯笼被挂上一扇素门。

branches.en: The first sense is colour and ornaments added for beauty.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是为好看而添上的颜色与饰物。

branches.en: The second sense is the same addition made permanent in a house.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把同样的添置固定进房子里。

branches.en: The third sense adds honour instead of colour.
branches.cn: 第三个义项添的不是颜色，而是荣誉。

branches.en: A festival room and a renovated room are both dressed.
branches.cn: 过节的房间和翻新的房间，都算穿上了衣服。

branches.en: Beauty and honour were one idea in the Latin source.
branches.cn: 在拉丁源头里，美与荣誉本是一个念头。

intro.en: Decorate gives decoration, decorative and decorator, the whole dressing family.
intro.cn: decorate 长出 decoration、decorative 和 decorator，是一家与「装扮」有关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decus, honour and beauty, with decorare meaning to adorn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decus（荣誉与美），decorare 意为装点。

items.example: They decorated the hall in one day.
items.exampleCN: 他们用一天装饰好了大厅。

items.meaning: an ornament or the act of adorning
items.example: The decorations came down in January.
items.exampleCN: 装饰品在一月被取了下来。

items.example: The decorator chose a warm white.
items.exampleCN: 装饰工挑了一种暖白色。

items.meaning: the style of a room's fittings
items.example: The hotel has a simple decor.
items.exampleCN: 这家旅馆的装饰风格朴素。

items.example: A decorated tree stood by the window.
items.exampleCN: 窗边立着一棵装饰好的树。

items.example: They plan to redecorate in spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们打算春天重新装修。

latinEntries.example: Decus lies behind decorate and decorum.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decus 是 decorate 与 decorum 的来源。

definition_zh: 装饰性的；装饰用的
definition_en: made to look attractive rather than to be useful
core_image: 一只只能看、不能盛水的花碗
scene: 那只碗画着花，却从不拿来盛饭。The plate is purely decorative.
sceneCN: 这里 decorative 指「装饰性的」（第 1 个义项：只为好看而设）；句意是这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。

pos.zh: 装饰性的；装饰用的

senses.title: Made to be looked at
senses.definition: meant to please the eye rather than to serve a use
senses.definitionCN: 为了取悦眼睛，而不是为了实用
senses.example: The plate is purely decorative.
senses.exampleCN: 这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。
senses.why: Some things exist for the eye alone, and a word is needed to say so.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西只为眼睛存在，这就需要有个词来说明。

senses.title: Adding beauty to something
senses.definition: having the effect of making a place or an object prettier
senses.definitionCN: 起到让地方或物件变好看的效果
senses.example: The columns are decorative, not structural.
senses.exampleCN: 这些柱子只是装饰，并不承重。
senses.why: A part may look like support while doing only the work of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 一个部件看着像在承重，其实只负责好看。

intro.en: Decorative is Latin decorativus, having the power to adorn, from decorare.
intro.cn: decorative 是拉丁语 decorativus，意为「能装点的」，来自 decorare。

items.en: Decorativus meant having the power to adorn.
items.cn: decorativus 指具备装点的能力。

items.en: The -ivus suffix marked a quality rather than an act.
items.cn: -ivus 这个后缀标示的是一种性质，而非动作。

items.en: Décoratif described things that serve beauty.
items.cn: décoratif 形容为美服务的东西。

items.en: Decorative entered English with talk of the fine arts.
items.cn: decorative 随美术的话题进入英语。

items.en: It now separates the beautiful from the useful.
items.cn: 如今它把好看与实用区分开来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ative shape, and the meaning group names beauty with no use.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ative 的形状，近义组则都在说没有实用、只有好看的属性。

entries.definition: polite and correct in behaviour
copied from something else
likely to mislead
used as decoration
elaborate and not plain
pleasing to look at

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a bowl that is never used and end with a pillar that holds nothing up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只从不用来盛东西的碗开始，落到一根什么也不承的柱子。

normal.en: A decorative plate is beautiful and hungry.
normal.cn: 装饰盘很美，而且永远空着。

normal.en: Something decorative earns its place by being seen.
normal.cn: 装饰性的东西靠被看见来证明自己的位置。

normal.en: The prettiest buttons never do up anything.
normal.cn: 最好看的扣子，从来不扣住什么。

normal.en: Beauty that pretends to be structure is the best disguise.
normal.cn: 装成结构的美丽，是最好的伪装。

normal.en: Decorat- is the stem, -ive is the label, useful or not.
normal.cn: decorat- 是词干，-ive 是标签，至于有没有用另说。

abstract.en: Picture a painted bowl on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上摆着一只画了花的碗。

abstract.en: Picture a column that ends in mid air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根在半空中就断了的柱子。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain that hides nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一道什么也没遮住的帘子。

examples.en: The plate is purely decorative.
examples.cn: 这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。

examples.en: Decorative tiles cover the whole wall.
examples.cn: 装饰瓷砖铺满了整面墙。

examples.en: The handle is decorative but still works.
examples.cn: 这个把手是装饰性的，但仍然能用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decorative 记成「得客来秀」：de 是得，corative 听着像「客来秀」，客人来了就秀一秀那些只为好看的东西。

root: 来自拉丁语 decorativus（能装点的），后缀 -ivus 表示性质，源头仍是 decorare（装点）与 decus（美与荣誉）。十八世纪随美术话题进入英语，用来区分「只为好看」与「真正有用」。

sensesIntro.en: From an object made only for the eye, to a part that adds beauty without bearing weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从只为眼睛而做的物件，到只添美而不承重的部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted bowl that never holds water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只画着花、从不盛水的碗。

branches.en: The first sense is an object with no job but to be seen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是除被看见之外没有任务的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is a part that beautifies something else.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是给别的东西添美的部件。

branches.en: Both senses put beauty ahead of function.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把好看放在功用前面。

branches.en: One names a whole object, the other a part of one.
branches.cn: 一个指整个物件，一个指物件的一部分。

branches.en: A decorative part often pretends to be a working one.
branches.cn: 装饰性的部件，常常装成有用的样子。

intro.en: Decorative is the adjective of quality in the decorate family.
intro.cn: decorative 是 decorate 一族里表示性质的那个形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin suffix -ivus marks a quality, added to decorare, to adorn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁后缀 -ivus 表示性质，加在 decorare（装点）之上。

items.example: A decorative arch frames the door.
items.exampleCN: 一道装饰性的拱框住了门。

items.example: They decorate the shop each winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年冬天装饰店铺。
装饰工建议用更暖的颜色。
石头被摆成装饰的样子。

items.example: They praised the decorativeness of the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他们称赞这道门的装饰性。
没有装饰的墙显得冷峻。

definition_zh: v. 使分离；使脱钩；解除（两者间的）关联；减弱（联系）
definition_en: to separate two things that were joined or linked, so that each can act on its own
core_image: 两节挂在一起的车厢，挂钩被打开，各自停在不同的轨道上
scene: 工程师把两个系统分开。They decided to decouple the two systems.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：decouple 指解除两者的连接；句意是他们决定把两个系统分离开。

pos.zh: 使分离；使脱钩；解除关联；减弱联系

senses.title: Unhook two parts
senses.definition: to physically unfasten two joined parts
senses.definitionCN: 把连接在一起的两部分拆开
senses.example: They decided to decouple the two systems.
senses.exampleCN: 他们决定把两个系统分离开。
senses.why: A hook opened between two carriages.
senses.whyCN: 两节车厢之间的挂钩被打开。

senses.title: Break a link between trends
senses.definition: to make two things stop rising or falling together
senses.definitionCN: 让两件事不再同步升降
senses.example: The country decoupled growth from emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 该国让经济增长与排放脱钩。
senses.why: Two lines on a chart pulled apart.
senses.whyCN: 图表上的两条线被拉开。

senses.title: Reduce a dependency
senses.definition: to weaken the dependence of one part on another
senses.definitionCN: 削弱一部分对另一部分的依赖
senses.example: We decoupled the service from the database.
senses.exampleCN: 我们减弱了服务对数据库的依赖。
senses.why: A rope slackened until each end stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 绳子松到两端各自立住。

intro.en: Decouple is de- plus couple, from Latin copula, a bond or tie.
intro.cn: decouple 由 de- 加 couple 构成，couple 源自拉丁语 copula，意为纽带或连接。

items.en: Copula meant a bond or a tie.
items.cn: copula 意为纽带或连接。

items.en: Couple named two things joined together.
items.cn: couple 指连在一起的两个东西。

items.en: Couple entered English for a paired set.
items.cn: 十四世纪 couple 以成对义进入英语。

items.en: Couple became a verb for joining parts.
items.cn: 十八世纪 couple 成为连接部件的动词。

items.en: Decouple was coined for unhooking vehicles.
items.cn: 二十世纪 decouple 为摘挂车辆而造出。

items.en: Decouple now names economic and software separation.
items.cn: 如今 decouple 指经济与软件上的分离。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the couple family; the near-meaning group names ways of pulling things apart.
note.cn: 形近组同属 couple 家族；近义组都是「把东西拉开」的说法。

entries.definition: To join or link two things together.
To disconnect two joined parts.
A device that links two parts.
To move things apart from each other.
To remove something from what it is attached to.
To break a connection between things.
To cut something off completely.

normalIntro.en: Decouple is de- plus couple: undo the pairing.
normalIntro.cn: decouple 就是 de- 加 couple：把成对的连接解开。

normal.en: A couple is two joined things.
normal.cn: couple 是连在一起的两个东西。

normal.en: De- takes the joining away.
normal.cn: de- 把连接去掉。

normal.en: Decouple opens the hook.
normal.cn: decouple 把挂钩打开。

normal.en: Two carriages roll apart.
normal.cn: 两节车厢各自滚开。

normal.en: Two chart lines stop moving together.
normal.cn: 图表上两条线不再同步移动。

abstract.en: A hook opened between two carriages.
abstract.cn: 两节车厢之间的挂钩被打开。

abstract.en: Two lines on a chart pulled apart.
abstract.cn: 图表上的两条线被拉开。

abstract.en: A rope slackened until each end stands alone.
abstract.cn: 绳子松到两端各自立住。

examples.en: The engineer decoupled the engine from the gearbox.
examples.cn: 工程师把发动机与变速箱分离开。

examples.en: Prices decoupled from wages last year.
examples.cn: 去年物价与工资脱钩了。

examples.en: We want to decouple these two modules.
examples.cn: 我们想把这两个模块解耦。

dict_mnemonic.text: decouple 谐音「弟卡剖」——不如记 de（去掉）＋ couple（一对、连接）＝把这一对拆开，「使分离、脱钩」。

root: 拉丁语 copula（纽带）→ 古法语 couple（一对）→ 英语 couple（连接）→ decouple（使分离）

sensesIntro.en: One opened hook: two parts, two trends and two dependencies.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被打开的挂钩：两个部件、两条趋势与两种依赖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hook opened between two carriages so each stands on its own
core.cn: 核心意象：两节车厢之间的挂钩被打开，各自独立

branches.en: A hook opened between two carriages.
branches.cn: 两节车厢之间的挂钩被打开。

branches.en: Two lines on a chart pulled apart.
branches.cn: 图表上的两条线被拉开。

branches.en: A rope slackened until each end stands alone.
branches.cn: 绳子松到两端各自立住。

branches.en: Both remove a physical or structural tie between parts.
branches.cn: 两者都去掉部件之间物理或结构上的纽带。

branches.en: Both let one side change without dragging the other.
branches.cn: 两者都让一方变化时不再拖着另一方。

intro.en: Decouple is de- plus couple; the bond root builds many joining and parting words.
intro.cn: decouple 由 de- 加 couple 构成；纽带词根造出许多连接与分离的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin copula means a bond and jungere means to join.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 copula 意为纽带，jungere 意为连接。

definition_zh: 减少；降低；减少量
definition_en: to become or make something smaller in number or size
core_image: 水位在杯壁上一点点退下去
scene: 关掉几盏灯之后，电费单上的数字小了不少。The number of visitors decreased in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 decrease 指「减少」（第 1 个义项：数量变小）；句意是冬天游客数量减少了。

pos.zh: 减少；降低
减少；减少量

senses.title: Become smaller by itself
senses.definition: to fall in number, size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量、大小或额度下降
senses.example: The number of visitors decreased in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天游客数量减少了。
senses.why: A quantity that shrinks leaves a smaller mark on the page.
senses.whyCN: 缩小的数量，在纸上留下的痕迹也小了一圈。

senses.title: Bring something down
senses.definition: to make a number or level go down on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地让数字或水平降下来
senses.example: The factory decreased its water use by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把用水量减少了一半。
senses.why: The same change can happen by itself or by a hand.
senses.whyCN: 同样的变化，可以自己发生，也可以由一只手推动。

senses.title: The size of a fall
senses.definition: the measured amount by which something falls
senses.definitionCN: 测量出来的下降幅度
senses.example: There was a small decrease in prices last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月价格有小幅下降。
senses.why: Once a fall is measured, it becomes a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: 一次下跌一旦被量出来，就成了可以称呼的东西。

intro.en: Decrease came from Latin decrescere, to grow less, from crescere, to grow.
intro.cn: decrease 来自拉丁语 decrescere（变少），源于 crescere（生长）。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow or increase.
items.cn: crescere 指生长、增加。

items.en: Decrescere meant to grow less or shrink.
items.cn: decrescere 指长得更少、缩小。

items.en: Decroistre carried the same sense into French.
items.cn: decroistre 把同样的意思带进法语。

items.en: Decrease entered English as a verb of shrinking.
items.cn: decrease 作为表示缩小的动词进入英语。

items.en: The noun came later, naming the size of the fall.
items.cn: 名词用法更晚，用来指下降的幅度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the de- opening, and the meaning group all describe things going down.
note.cn: 形近组都以 de- 开头，近义组则都在说往下走。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with water slipping down a glass and end with a measured fall on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从杯壁上退下去的水开始，落到纸面上被量出来的一次下跌。

normal.en: Water leaves a glass without a sound and the mark stays.
normal.cn: 水悄无声息地离开杯子，痕迹留下了。

normal.en: Turning off lights is decrease you can see on a bill.
normal.cn: 关灯这件事，能在账单上看见。

normal.en: Growth and decrease use the same root, only the direction differs.
normal.cn: 增加和减少同出一个词根，只差一个方向。

normal.en: Decrease by half is easier to say than to do.
normal.cn: 「减半」说起来，比做起来容易得多。

normal.en: A decrease is a fall small enough to measure.
normal.cn: 减少量就是小到可以量出来的那次下跌。

abstract.en: Picture a ring left on a glass by lower water.
abstract.cn: 想象杯壁上被退下去的水留下的一圈印。

abstract.en: Picture a meter turning back one number.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表往回退了一个数。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaving a hall one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象人群一排一排地离开大厅。

examples.en: The number of visitors decreased in winter.
examples.cn: 冬天游客数量减少了。

examples.en: We must decrease the amount of waste we produce.
examples.cn: 我们必须减少产生的垃圾量。

examples.en: There was a slight decrease in traffic after the new road opened.
examples.cn: 新路开通后交通量略有下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decrease 记成「得亏少」：de 是得，crease 像「亏少」，账上亏得少了，就是数量在往下走。

root: 源自拉丁语 decrescere（变少），由 de（向下）与 crescere（生长）构成，字面意思就是「往下长」。十五世纪作为动词进入英语，名词用法出现得更晚，用来指下降的幅度。

sensesIntro.en: From a number falling by itself, to a hand pushing it down, to the measured size of the fall.
sensesIntro.cn: 从数字自行下降，到一只手把它按下去，再到这次下降被量出的幅度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water slipping down the inside of a glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿着杯子内壁缓缓退下。

branches.en: The first sense is a quantity going down without help.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是数量自己往下走。

branches.en: The second sense is someone pushing the quantity down.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是有人把数量按下去。

branches.en: The third sense turns the fall into a figure on paper.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这次下跌变成纸上的一个数字。

branches.en: The change looks the same whoever causes it.
branches.cn: 不管是谁造成的，这个变化看起来一样。

branches.en: A trend is only many small decreases added together.
branches.cn: 所谓趋势，不过是许多次小幅减少加在一起。

intro.en: Decrease shares its stem with increase, concrete and crescent: all grow from crescere.
intro.cn: decrease 与 increase、concrete、crescent 共用一个词干，都从 crescere 长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is crescere, to grow, with the prefix de- pulling it downward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 crescere（生长），前缀 de- 把它往下拉。

items.exampleCN: 他们看着不断减少的数字。

items.example: Each step is a decrement of one.
There was a decrease in noise.
The sharp decrease surprised the bank.
items.exampleCN: 急剧减少让银行吃了一惊。

items.example: Bird numbers are on the decrease.
Good sleep decreases the risk of illness.
items.exampleCN: 好的睡眠能降低患病风险。

latinEntries.example: Crescere gives English increase and decrease.
latinEntries.exampleCN: crescere 给英语带来 increase 和 decrease。

definition_zh: n. 法令；政令；（法院的）判决、裁定 v. 裁定；颁布法令；命令
definition_en: an official order or decision, especially one made by a ruler or a court
core_image: 一张盖着印章的纸从高处递下来，下面的人只能照办
scene: 法院昨天签发了那道裁定。The court issued a decree yesterday.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：decree 指法院的裁定；句意是法院昨天签发了那道裁定。

pos.zh: 法令；政令；判决；裁定
裁定；颁布法令；命令

senses.title: An official order
senses.definition: an official order given by a ruler or government
senses.definitionCN: 统治者或政府发布的正式命令
senses.example: The king signed a royal decree.
senses.exampleCN: 国王签署了一道王室敕令。
senses.why: A stamp on paper that everyone must obey.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的印章让所有人必须服从。

senses.title: A court decision
senses.definition: a judgement or order made by a court
senses.definitionCN: 法院作出的判决或命令
senses.example: The court issued a decree yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 法院昨天签发了那道裁定。
senses.why: A bench turning a dispute into a rule.
senses.whyCN: 法官席把争执变成一条规则。

senses.title: A divorce final order
senses.definition: the final legal order that ends a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 正式结束婚姻的最终法律命令
senses.example: The decree absolute arrived by post.
senses.exampleCN: 离婚终判书邮寄到了。
senses.why: A knot cut by a written line.
senses.whyCN: 一个结被一行文字剪断。

senses.title: Order by authority
senses.definition: to order something officially with authority
senses.definitionCN: 以权威正式发布命令
senses.example: The governor decreed a day of mourning.
senses.exampleCN: 州长下令举行哀悼日。
senses.why: One voice making a rule for many.
senses.whyCN: 一个声音为许多人定下规则。

intro.en: Decree comes from Latin decretum, a decision, from decernere, to decide.
intro.cn: decree 源自拉丁语 decretum（决定），来自 decernere（判定）。

items.en: Cernere meant to separate or sift.
items.cn: cernere 意为分开或筛。

items.en: Decernere meant to decide by separating options.
items.cn: decernere 意为通过区分选项来判定。

items.en: Decretum named what had been decided.
items.cn: decretum 指已经判定的事。

items.en: Decret carried the sense into French.
items.cn: decret 把这个含义带入法语。

items.en: Decree entered English for an official order.
items.cn: 十四世纪 decree 以正式命令义进入英语。

items.en: Decree was standard in divorce and church law.
items.cn: 十九世纪 decree 是离婚法与教会法的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dec- opening; the near-meaning group names official orders.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dec- 的开头；近义组都是「正式命令」的说法。

entries.definition: To choose after thinking.
Old and in very bad condition.
A letter containing a papal decision.
An order given by a person in authority.
A law made by a local authority.
An official decision made by a judge.
An official order to do something.

normalIntro.en: Decree is de- plus cernere, to sift: a decision sifted out and made binding.
normalIntro.cn: decree 就是 de- 加 cernere（筛）：筛出来的决定，并且必须执行。

normal.en: Cernere means to sift in Latin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛。

normal.en: Decernere means to decide.
normal.cn: decernere 意为判定。

normal.en: A decree is the sifted result.
normal.cn: decree 是筛出来的结果。

normal.en: A stamp makes it binding.
normal.cn: 印章让它必须执行。

normal.en: A court decree ends a case.
normal.cn: 法院裁定结束一个案件。

abstract.en: A stamp on paper that everyone must obey.
abstract.cn: 纸上的印章让所有人必须服从。

abstract.en: A bench turning a dispute into a rule.
abstract.cn: 法官席把争执变成一条规则。

abstract.en: A knot cut by a written line.
abstract.cn: 一个结被一行文字剪断。

examples.en: The government ruled by decree for a year.
examples.cn: 政府以政令方式统治了一年。

examples.en: They decreed that the park would close at dusk.
examples.cn: 他们下令公园黄昏时关闭。

examples.en: The decree was published in the gazette.
examples.cn: 那道法令刊登在公报上。

dict_mnemonic.text: decree 谐音「弟克瑞」——不如记 de（彻底）＋ cree（想成「刻」）＝把决定刻在纸上再盖章，「法令、裁定」。

sensesIntro.en: One stamped paper: an order, a judgement, a divorce and a command.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一张盖章的纸：政令、判决、离婚终判与命令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped paper handed down from above that everyone below must obey
core.cn: 核心意象：一张盖章的纸从高处递下，下面的人必须照办

branches.en: A stamp on paper that everyone must obey.
branches.cn: 纸上的印章让所有人必须服从。

branches.en: A bench turning a dispute into a rule.
branches.cn: 法官席把争执变成一条规则。

branches.en: A knot cut by a written line.

branches.en: One voice making a rule for many.

branches.en: All four are a decision that has been made binding on others.
branches.cn: 四者都是已经对他人产生约束力的决定。

intro.en: Decree is de- plus cernere; the sifting and cutting roots build many decision words.
intro.cn: decree 由 de- 加 cernere 构成；筛与切这两个词根造出许多决定类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere means to sift and caedere means to cut.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛，caedere 意为切。

definition_zh: adj. 破旧的；年久失修的；衰老的；老朽的
definition_en: old and in very bad condition, worn out by age or long use
core_image: 一栋木房子的梁柱被岁月压弯，墙皮一片片往下掉
scene: 那座老桥在风里晃。The decrepit bridge swayed in the wind.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：decrepit 指年久失修；句意是那座破旧的桥在风中摇晃。

pos.zh: 破旧的；年久失修的；衰老的；老朽的

senses.title: Worn out by age
senses.definition: in very bad condition because of long use or age
senses.definitionCN: 因长期使用或年久而状况很差
senses.example: The decrepit bridge swayed in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 那座破旧的桥在风中摇晃。
senses.why: A frame bent under the weight of years.
senses.whyCN: 一副被岁月重量压弯的骨架。

senses.title: Feeble with old age
senses.definition: weak and broken down because of being very old
senses.definitionCN: 因年迈而虚弱衰败
senses.example: A decrepit dog lay by the stove.
senses.exampleCN: 一条衰老的狗躺在炉子边。
senses.why: A body whose springs have lost their push.
senses.whyCN: 一具弹簧失去推力的身体。

senses.title: Falling apart
senses.definition: so neglected that it is close to collapse
senses.definitionCN: 因疏于维护而接近倒塌
senses.example: The decrepit factory was finally torn down.
senses.exampleCN: 那座破败的工厂终于被拆掉。
senses.why: A wall held up only by habit.
senses.whyCN: 一堵只靠惯性立着的墙。

intro.en: Decrepit comes from Latin decrepitus, broken down by age, from de- plus crepare, to crack.
intro.cn: decrepit 源自拉丁语 decrepitus（因年老而衰败），由 de- 加 crepare（裂开、作响）构成。

items.en: Crepare meant to crack or rattle.
items.cn: crepare 意为裂开或作响。

items.en: Decrepitus described someone broken by age.
items.cn: decrepitus 形容被岁月压垮的人。

items.en: Decrepite was an early English spelling.
items.cn: decrepite 是早期英语拼法。

items.en: Decrepit settled as the modern spelling.
items.cn: 十六世纪 decrepit 定为现代拼法。

items.en: Decrepit was used for buildings and machines.
items.cn: 十八世纪 decrepit 用于建筑与机器。

items.en: Decrepit became common in urban reporting.
items.cn: 二十世纪 decrepit 常见于城市报道。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dec- opening; the near-meaning group names things worn out by time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dec- 的开头；近义组都是「被时间磨坏」的说法。

normal.en: De- means all the way down.

normal.en: Decrepit is cracked by years.
normal.cn: decrepit 是被岁月裂开的。

normal.en: An old bridge creaks and sways.
normal.cn: 老桥吱呀作响、摇摇晃晃。

normal.en: A decrepit wall sheds its skin.
normal.cn: 破败的墙一片片掉皮。

abstract.en: A frame bent under the weight of years.

abstract.en: A wall held up only by habit.

examples.en: They live in a decrepit flat above the shop.
examples.cn: 他们住在商店楼上一套破旧的公寓里。

examples.en: The decrepit bus broke down twice.
examples.cn: 那辆破旧的大巴抛锚了两次。

examples.en: He looked decrepit after the long illness.
examples.cn: 久病之后他显得很衰老。

dict_mnemonic.text: decrepit 谐音「弟克瑞皮特」——不如记 de（彻底）＋ crepit（裂响，像 crack）＝彻底裂到掉皮，「破旧的、衰老的」。

root: 拉丁语 crepare（裂开、作响）→ decrepitus（因年老而衰败）→ 英语 decrepit

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden frame bent by years until the skin falls off

branches.en: A frame bent under the weight of years.

intro.en: Decrepit is de- plus crepare; the cracking and falling roots build many decay words.

latinIntro.en: Latin crepare means to crack and ruere means to fall down.

definition_zh: v. 把…献给；把（时间、精力）用于；致力；题献；为…举行落成礼
definition_en: to give time, effort or yourself entirely to a purpose, or to offer something to a person or cause
core_image: 一个人把整段人生像一本书一样放到某个目标的祭坛上
scene: 她把一生都献给了教学。She dedicated her life to teaching.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：dedicate 指把时间精力全部投入；句意是她把一生献给了教学。

pos.zh: 把…献给；把…用于；致力；题献；为…举行落成礼

senses.title: Give yourself to a cause
senses.definition: to give all your time and energy to a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把全部时间与精力投入某个目标
senses.example: She dedicated her life to teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一生献给了教学。
senses.why: A whole life placed on one altar.
senses.whyCN: 整整一生被放到一座祭坛上。

senses.title: Set something apart for a use
senses.definition: to reserve something for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某物留作特定用途
senses.example: The room is dedicated to quiet study.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间专供安静自习。
senses.why: A space fenced off for one task.
senses.whyCN: 一块被围起来只做一件事的空间。

senses.title: Offer a book to someone
senses.definition: to write that a book or song is offered to a person
senses.definitionCN: 在书上写明把作品献给某人
senses.example: He dedicated the novel to his mother.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这部小说题献给母亲。
senses.why: A name written on the first page as a gift.
senses.whyCN: 第一页上写着一个名字，当作礼物。

senses.title: Open a building formally
senses.definition: to hold a ceremony marking a building as ready for use
senses.definitionCN: 举行仪式宣布建筑正式启用

senses.exampleCN: 市长为新图书馆主持落成礼。
senses.why: A ribbon cut and a door handed over.
senses.whyCN: 彩带剪断，门被交出去。

intro.en: Dedicate comes from Latin dedicare, to proclaim, from de- plus dicare, to make known.
intro.cn: dedicate 源自拉丁语 dedicare（宣告奉献），由 de- 加 dicare（宣告）构成。

items.en: Dicare meant to make known or proclaim.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告、使知晓。

items.en: Dicere meant to say, the same family as dicare.
items.cn: dicere 意为说，与 dicare 同族。

items.en: Dedicare meant to devote something to a god.
items.cn: dedicare 意为把某物奉献给神。

items.en: Dedicate entered English for offering to a patron.
items.cn: 十五世纪 dedicate 以献给赞助人义进入英语。

items.en: Dedicate was used for formal opening ceremonies.
items.cn: 十七世纪 dedicate 用于正式落成仪式。

items.en: Dedicate widened to giving time and effort.
items.cn: 十九世纪 dedicate 扩展到投入时间与精力。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dic- saying family; the near-meaning group names giving yourself to something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dic-（说）家族；近义组都是「把自己交给某事」的说法。

To show or point something out.
Fine and easily broken or harmed.
